sections.vendors: No new factory list has surfaced — the published version is still dated 1 April 2026 (asosplc.com/media/cmzk3m5n/factory-list-april-2026.pdf), meaning the quarterly refresh is now roughly five months overdue against ASOS's own every-three-months cadence. Worth checking asosplc.com weekly for a Q3/Q4 edition covering China, Turkey, Bangladesh and India.
sections.sourcing: ASOS's 24 September pre-close trading update (FY ended 30 August 2026) credited 'improved sourcing' alongside stronger full-price sell-through for pushing adjusted gross margin above its 50% medium-term target — into the upper half of guidance. The update also reiterated flexibility to tweak sourcing and distribution (many US orders now fulfilled from European warehouses) to manage tariff exposure, and confirmed continued work to trim own-brand SKU count toward a 6,000-6,500 target range.
sections.strategy: The pre-close update showed sequential GMV improvement every quarter through FY26, returning to low-single-digit growth in Q4 — the first quarter-on-quarter active-customer growth since Q2 FY22 — attributed to progress on three pillars: Relevant Fashion Product, Inspirational Shopping Experience and Efficient Operating Model. Concretely, ASOS added roughly 30 net new Partner Brands and posted a record S/S26 sell-through rate (+4pp year-on-year). Net debt fell to ~£110m (from £184.7m a year earlier). Full FY26 results are due 5 November.
sections.pricing: Standard autumn promotional cadence continued — 20-25% off codes on app orders circulating widely across affiliate/coupon sites through late September, consistent with ASOS's markdown-light, promo-heavy positioning. No structural pricing news this week.
sections.launches: ASOS launched a new autumn brand campaign ('behind the style') and confirmed ASOS Magazine and its London Fashion Week experience will relaunch this month, with editorial leadership and cover talent still to be announced.
sections.gossip: Shares rallied on the 24 September trading update, and analyst sentiment has turned more constructive: consensus price targets have moved up (roughly £3.31 to £3.51), with some estimates lifted toward £4.00 and FY26 per-share losses forecast to narrow from -£0.599 to -£0.434. Shares traded around 421.5p as of 21 September.
soWhat: Margin gains explicitly tied to 'improved sourcing' signal ASOS is still squeezing cost and terms from its vendor base even as sales recover — expect continued pressure on FOB pricing rather than a loosening once volumes return.

The SKU-reduction push toward 6,000-6,500 own-brand lines means a shrinking, more concentrated vendor list going forward; being one of the surviving core suppliers matters more than winning one-off orders.

A factory list now five months overdue is unusual even by ASOS's recent slow-refresh pattern — when it lands, compare it closely against April's version for tier-1 exits, since a lagged publication sometimes coincides with larger-than-usual supplier churn.
